review:
Nine Queens is an argentinian movie that revolves around the hustles of two con artists trying to take advantages and make some quick money in clever ways. Juan (Gastón Pauls) starts the film by himself, playing a simple but deceptive con on a cashier, when it doesn't go exactly as expected, it's Marcos (Ricardo Darín) that appears to help him. And with that, this partnership between the two are born and carries on for the rest of the film.

Their partnership is not a simple one. At moments, Marcos acts as Mentor for Juan. Sometimes they act as old friends that have swindling as common hobby. But most of the times, both of them acts with certain suspicion of one another, and I feel that we as viewers get to feel that same suspicion not just for them, but also for other characters that are involved. And it's those suspicions that keeps us guessing who is taking advantage of who, where it will all end and what's the next clever curve ball the director will throw at us.
